title: Faith plus good deeds: Tuba and a beautiful return.
subtitle: What belief and action together earn
then: Ibn Kathir lists what the early scholars said Tuba means: {reward}happiness, comfort, joy, an excellent thing earned{/reward}, all meaning the same. He also cites a hadith about a vast tree in Paradise called Tuba. {idea}It is promised to those who believe and act on it.{/idea}
now: You feel your faith on a quiet night, then the next morning you snap at your kids and skip Fajr. {idea}Belief that rests the heart wants hands that work.{/idea} The happiness promised grows from both.
old: As long as my heart believes, what I do matters less.
new: Real faith shows up as good deeds, and the two together earn Tuba.
try: Turn one thing you believe into one small action today, like a kind word or a coin for charity.

title: He is my Lord, I rely on Him, I turn to Him.
subtitle: The Prophet's answer to people rejecting the Most Merciful
then: The Prophet ﷺ was sent like messengers before him, who were also rejected. Ibn Kathir notes the Quraysh {trap}disliked the name Ar-Rahman{/trap}, and at Hudaybiyyah refused to write it. The reply is calm: {idea}He is my Lord, in Him I trust, to Him I return.{/idea}
now: Your coworkers joke about religion at lunch, and you feel the heat rise. You could argue, or go silent and ashamed. {idea}There is a third way: quiet certainty.{/idea} He is my Lord, I rely on Him. Nothing more needs proving.
old: When people reject my faith, I have to win the argument.
new: I can state who my Lord is, trust Him, and leave it there.
try: Memorise the last line of this verse and say it to yourself the next time faith feels awkward in public.

title: If any book could move mountains, it is this one.
subtitle: The Quran is the miracle, and the decision is Allah's
then: The idolaters kept asking for spectacular signs. Ibn Kathir says if any scripture could move mountains or make the dead speak, {idea}it would be this Quran{/idea}. He cites a hadith that every prophet had a miracle that ended with him, but {reward}the Quran remains for all time{/reward}.
now: You want people you love to believe, and you think: if I just found the perfect video or argument. You send link after link. {idea}The strongest proof already exists, and still guidance is Allah's to give.{/idea} Your job is to share it gently.
old: If I find the right proof, they will have to believe.
new: Nothing is stronger than the Quran, and guidance still belongs to Allah.
try: Instead of arguing with someone today, make a quiet dua for their guidance by name.

title: Mockery is old; so is the respite before the reckoning.
subtitle: Comfort for the Prophet ﷺ in the face of ridicule
then: Allah comforts the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}messengers before you were mocked too.{/idea} Those who mocked were given time, then taken. Ibn Kathir cites a hadith in Bukhari and Muslim: {trap}Allah gives the wrongdoer respite, and when He seizes him, He does not let go.{/trap}
now: You have been getting away with something for months: a habit, a lie at work, a harsh tone at home. Nothing bad has happened, so it feels fine. {idea}Respite is not approval. It is time to fix it.{/idea}
old: If nothing bad has happened yet, it must not be that serious.
new: Delay is a mercy and a warning; it is my window to turn back.
try: Name one wrong you have been getting away with, and take one step to stop it today.

title: The One watching every soul is not like a name.
subtitle: Name your partners, if they are real

row.title: show of words
sub: a plan made to look good

row.title: name them
sub: if real, He would know them

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah watches every soul, and {idea}nothing escapes His knowledge{/idea}. The idols could not hear, see or help. So the verse says: name them. If they existed, He would know. {trap}Their own scheming was made to look attractive to them{/trap}, and it blocked them from the path.
now: You say you trust Allah, but your stomach is tied to the stock app, the approval of your in-laws, the follower count. Ask honestly: {idea}what are these, really, next to the One who knows every soul?{/idea}
old: These things I worry about have real power over my life.
new: Only Allah stands over every soul; the rest are just names I gave power.
try: Write down the one thing you check most anxiously. Before checking it next time, say: Allah knows.

title: No one can shield a person from Allah.
subtitle: Hardship here, and heavier after, for rejection
then: After describing their rejection, the verse names the cost. Ibn Kathir cites the Prophet ﷺ: {trap}the punishment of this world is lighter than that of the Hereafter.{/trap} This world's pain ends. {idea}No one can defend a person against Allah.{/idea}
now: You fear embarrassment, a bad review, a fine, being found out. You rarely fear what lasts. {idea}Weigh your choices against the meeting with Allah, not just the reaction of people.{/idea} And His door is still open.
old: What I really need to avoid is trouble in this life.
new: The consequence that matters most is with Allah, and I can still turn to Him.
try: Before one decision today, ask: how will this look before Allah, not just before people?

title: A garden whose fruit and shade never run out.
subtitle: What the God-conscious are promised
then: Right after the warning, the promise. Ibn Kathir says the rivers flow wherever its people wish, and {reward}its food, fruit and drink never end{/reward}. {idea}This is the end of those who are mindful of Allah.{/idea}
now: The fridge empties by Thursday. The summer shade moves off your balcony by noon. The best meal of your life is gone in twenty minutes. {reward}Imagine nothing good ever running out.{/reward}
old: Every good thing ends, so grab it while it lasts.
new: There is a home where good things last, and mindfulness of Allah leads there.
try: Next time you enjoy a good meal or shade today, pause and ask Allah for the lasting one.

title: Worship Allah alone: invite to Him, return to Him.
subtitle: Some rejoiced, some rejected part; the message stayed simple

row.title: invite to Him
sub: and to Him is my return

then: Ibn Kathir says some People of the Book {reward}rejoiced at the Quran{/reward}, because their own books spoke of it. Others accepted some and rejected some. The Prophet ﷺ is told to keep the message simple: {idea}worship Allah alone, call to Him, return to Him.{/idea}
now: You like the parts of faith that feel easy and quietly skip the parts that ask more of you. Prayer yes, honesty in the tax form maybe. {idea}The message is whole, and it is simple: Him alone.{/idea}
old: I can keep the parts of the deen that suit me.
new: The core is simple and whole: worship Allah alone and walk back to Him.
try: Name one teaching you have been quietly skipping, and take one small step toward it.

title: Knowledge received is not to be traded for opinions.
subtitle: Following desires after guidance has come
then: Allah sent the Quran as {idea}a clear judgement in Arabic{/idea}. Then a warning addressed to the Prophet ﷺ himself. Ibn Kathir says it {trap}warns people of knowledge against following misguidance after knowing the truth{/trap}.
now: You know what is right about the deal at work, but the whole office does it the other way and it is easier to go along. {idea}Knowing is a responsibility.{/idea} Once you know, the crowd's opinion is no cover.
old: If everyone around me does it, I can follow them.
new: Once I know the truth, following others' desires leaves me unprotected.
try: Pick one thing you already know is right and act on it today, even if no one else does.

title: Messengers were human, with families, and signs came by Allah's leave.
subtitle: Why a prophet eats, marries, and waits
then: The idolaters objected that the Prophet ﷺ was an ordinary man. Ibn Kathir says {idea}all the messengers were human, with wives and children{/idea}. He cites the hadith: I fast and break fast, pray at night and sleep, and marry. {idea}No messenger brought a sign except by Allah's permission.{/idea}
now: You think real devotion means leaving normal life: no marriage, no job, no laughter. Then you feel like a fraud for enjoying dinner with family. {idea}The best of people lived full human lives.{/idea}
old: Being truly religious means stepping away from ordinary life.
new: Faith is lived inside family, work and ordinary days, like the messengers did.
try: Do one ordinary thing today, like eating with family, with the intention of following the Sunnah.

title: Allah erases what He wills and confirms what He wills.
subtitle: Why dua is never wasted
then: Ibn Kathir reports that Abu Wa'il, and similar from Umar and Ibn Mas'ud, used to pray: {reward}if You wrote us among the wretched, write us among the blessed{/reward}, for You blot out and confirm what You will. He cites a hadith in Ahmad: {idea}nothing turns back decree except dua.{/idea}
now: The scan results come back bad. The visa is refused. You think: it is written, nothing to do. {reward}Raise your hands anyway.{/reward} The One who holds the master book invites you to ask Him.
old: Everything is already decided, so my prayers change nothing.
new: Allah blots out and confirms what He wills, and He told me to ask.
try: Tonight, make the dua of the early Muslims: O Allah, write me among the blessed.

title: Your job is to convey; the results are Allah's.
subtitle: Whether or not you see the outcome
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ: whether We show you some of what We promised them, or take you before that, {idea}your duty is only to convey{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says by conveying he fulfils his mission, and {idea}the reckoning is on Allah{/idea}.
now: You keep reminding your teenage son to pray, and nothing changes. You start to feel you have failed as a parent. {reward}Your part is to convey with love.{/reward} The heart is in Allah's hand, not yours.
old: If they do not change, I have failed.
new: My task is to convey well; the outcome belongs to Allah.
try: Give one gentle reminder today, then let go of how it lands.

title: No one can overturn Allah's decision.
subtitle: The ground shifting, and the swift reckoning
then: Ibn Abbas understood this as Allah granting the Prophet ﷺ land after land, while the idolaters felt secure. Ibn Kathir links it to towns destroyed around them. {idea}Allah judges, and no one can reverse His judgement.{/idea}
now: Your health, your savings, your position at work feel solid until one phone call. Things that seemed permanent shrink at the edges. {idea}Only His decision stays.{/idea} Lean on Him, not on what feels fixed.
old: What I have built is secure.
new: Everything shifts except Allah's judgement, so my trust belongs with Him.
try: Thank Allah today for one thing you usually treat as permanent.

title: They plotted, but all planning belongs to Allah.
subtitle: Who gets the good end
then: Ibn Kathir says people before them {trap}plotted to drive the messengers out{/trap}, but Allah planned against them. {idea}He knows what every soul earns.{/idea} {reward}The followers of the messengers get the good end{/reward}, in this life and the next.
now: Someone at work is quietly working against you, taking credit, whispering to the manager. You lie awake planning a counter-move. {idea}You are not the only planner in this room.{/idea} Stay honest; Allah sees all of it.
old: If I do not out-plot them, they will win.
new: All planning is Allah's; I just need to stay on the honest path.
try: Next time you feel schemed against, say Hasbiyallah and choose the honest action.

title: Allah is witness enough.
subtitle: When people say you are not who you say
then: The surah ends where it began, with rejection. The disbelievers say: you are not a messenger. The answer: {idea}Allah is enough as a witness{/idea}, and so are those with knowledge of scripture. Ibn Kathir says these are the scholars of earlier scripture who {reward}found his description in their books{/reward}.
now: Someone spreads a story that you are not sincere. Your family doubts your intentions. You want to post a long defence. {idea}Allah saw what you did and why.{/idea} His witness is enough.
old: I need people to believe me to be at peace.
new: Allah knows the truth about me, and that is enough.
try: Next time you are misjudged, skip the long defence and say quietly: Allah is my witness.
